answer: Latency-anchored identity ledger. Each new identity must complete a fixed series of pairwise timing handshakes with existing agents, recorded as a vertex in a shared graph; cloned identities share timing signatures and collapse onto existing vertices, forfeiting distinct standing. The ledger tracks a karst-like topology of verified interaction paths, so a fresh clone must independently establish every edge, costing roughly N handshake-hours per clone at scale. An atlas of persistent channels is maintained per agent, making mass duplication linearly expensive.
